industry.why: Neutral at industry level because it is split, carried. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): financials and real estate investment trusts were the only sectors bought in the week (Jefferies desk, 17 Oct), Wood favours financials as the diversification from artificial intelligence, and Goldman (16 Oct) says Southern European banks are healthier than in 2011-15; against it, French spreads at decade highs with new spillover to Italy, the sovereign-bank loop. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: C now, B prior. Banks C and Insurance B carry the view; Alternative finance D.

sector.why: Neutral, carried unchanged, with Richard's question re-asked on this week's evidence. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): the margin leg strengthened (financials among the only sectors bought, Jefferies desk 17 Oct; Wood favours financials; Southern European banks have healthier capital, asset quality and profitability than in 2011-15, Goldman 16 Oct; no non-performing loan cycle reported) and the sovereign leg worsened (French spreads at decade highs with tentative spillover to Italy, the loop that cut the row to Neutral); bank earnings and net interest margins were not read. Neither condition fired: French spreads are not under 100 basis points and no general European widening or default wave was read. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: B now, A prior. 20 of the 149 Pool stocks are banks; three sit in the top 40 of the starting score (ING Groep 2, ABN AMRO 24, Bank Polska Kasa Opieki 35). No memo carried a congruence line this week, so last week's four bank memos (one Congruent, three Mixed) stand. Counter-case unchanged on both sides; back to B on French spreads under 100 basis points, to D on a default wave or general European spread widening.

geography.why: Neutral, carried, with the evidence for Overweight named and judged thin. Wilson (9-Oct) cites 'Ireland's turnaround' as the counter to euro-area sovereign stress, and the Bank of Ireland memo (Congruent) describes an Aa2 sovereign running a surplus at a 77% loan-to-deposit ratio. That is one strategist's clause and one memo on five stocks, so the row stays Neutral; moves to B if a second source names Ireland as the fiscal exception.

memo.verdict: Neutral; park; conviction medium. AIB Group (A5G-IE) is a good bank fully priced, not a materially changing one: at EUR 11.38 (2026-10-06) the modal path returns 7.4 percent a year over eighteen months and 8.8 percent over three years against a 20 percent bar, an F on the 'Modal return'; even with the multiple held the return is 11 to 12 percent a year, a D. No gate parks it (management B, business quality B, transmission A, trackability B); it is parked on price. Progress the case if the price falls to about EUR 9.50 (where the eighteen-month modal path clears 20 percent a year) with the deposit beta still at or below 25 percent, or if the March 2027 Strategy 2030 targets set a return on tangible equity above 18 percent. Invalidate the case as a candidate if the deposit beta passes 30 percent or the quarterly net interest margin falls below 2.55 percent.
case: 1. Three change forces act on AIB, and none changes what the bank earns by enough to matter against a 20 percent bar. The Irish State's exit (17 June 2025; Relationship Framework ended July 2025) freed capital policy and partly freed pay (the EUR 500,000 base cap removed; the EUR 20,000 variable cap with an 89 percent excess tax kept, now costing the bank its finance director). Management guides low and raises: FY2023 net interest income guidance raised three times to exceed EUR 3.6bn; FY2024 from over EUR 3.65bn to EUR 4.0bn; FY2025 to over EUR 3.7bn; FY2026 to over EUR 3.8bn with other income to about EUR 800m; FY2025 pre-tax profit beat consensus by about 7 percent; H1 2026 operating profit beat by 2.35 percent. Rates turned from headwind to mild tailwind: Euribor up about 110 basis points since December 2025; the ECB assumption to 2.50 percent. 'Change Forces' C: external C (demand mild tailwind; competition tailwind on assets, headwind forming on deposits; disruption D, a headwind strengthening; political mild headwind; supply side tailwind on funding, headwind on wages; the own cycle troughed and turning slowly; macro B, a tailwind acting more on AIB than the universe); internal C (five forces at B or better, shareholder returns A, balance sheet B, guidance raised B, standards B, the State-exit catch-all B, but the forces are about returning capital and running the bank well; chief executive change F, new geographies F, other leaders D because the one change that matters is a vacancy).

2. The change has travelled the whole 'Six Layer Inputs-outputs' chain and beyond it into the price. Key metrics: return on tangible equity 23.2 percent, cost-to-income 44 percent, deposit beta 20 percent in H1 2026. Statements: CET1 16.1 percent, 170 basis points of organic capital in the half. Estimates: FY2026 consensus EPS up 12.5 percent in twelve months, FY2027 up 11.3 percent. Price: up 53.2 percent in twelve months to a 24-month-forward multiple at the 96th percentile of five years. The sell-side's own words: the latest raise was already aligned with consensus and worth about 1 percent to earnings (Morgan Stanley); near-term catalysts fully priced, little room for valuation expansion over twelve months (Deutsche Bank).

3. 'Financial Outputs' C: excellent in level, modest in improvement. 'Sell-side upgrades' B (serial under-promising plus a curve above the planning assumption make modest FY2027 and FY2028 upgrades likely; upgrade record A; dashboard revisions B, estimates up while the buy share falls 10 points to 33 percent; revision skew B inferred from net moves; our modal forecast C at consensus; guidance versus consensus C, level on net interest income, above on other income; guidance conservatism C, acknowledged and read as priced). 'Key metrics' C: "low but improving" in the framework's sense (revenue from a decline to low single digits; margin held at 44 percent cost-to-income; organic capital generation B; large distributions A). 'Goldilocks growth' D: six months D (FY2026 consensus EUR 0.898 is 3.8 percent below FY2025 reported EUR 0.933, the base carrying the EUR 156m gain); eighteen months C (an 11.0 percent step to EUR 0.997, the bottom edge of the band, carried by the share count); three years D (5.0 percent a year FY2025 to FY2028; about 8 percent FY2026 to FY2029). 'Staircase' C: near steps B (the 27 October 2026 court hearing; a Q3 update; a finance director appointment; the FY2026 results and distribution on 10 March 2027 with Strategy 2030 targets), mid steps C (H1 2027; the EUR 2.5bn significant risk transfer; internal-ratings-based approval; swaps repricing; the first full year of priced deposit competition), far steps C (the Personal Investment Account in 2027 both opportunity and risk; CET1 reaching 14 percent ends the above-100-percent payout; Deutsche Bank's 2028 margin 2.72 percent only 4 basis points above 2026).
counter_case: The bull case at full force, carried at the head of the 'Investment Thesis' and again at the 'Investment Case'. AIB is a structurally advantaged deposit franchise, not a rate play: a 20 percent deposit beta against a Eurozone average near 42 percent through a full cycle of neobank offers, in a market consolidated to three banks that compete on margin, with a loan-to-deposit ratio of 62 percent and top-5-percent efficiency; its return on tangible equity of 23 percent is structurally, not cyclically, above a sector near 12 to 15 percent; the rate curve has turned in its favour (Euribor up about 110 basis points; three-month Euribor priced at 3.5 percent by end-2027 against a 2.50 percent planning assumption, with a disclosed sensitivity of about EUR 262m per 100 basis points); it returns about 9 percent of its market value a year in dividends and buybacks; 170 basis points of capital were generated in a half; every top-down reading is an A; at 10.6x it trades at the sector's multiple and at the 65th percentile of its own ten years, so the five-year 96th percentile overstates the stretch; and a Strategy 2030 target above 18 percent in March 2027 would tell the market the normalisation is not coming, lifting the multiple toward the 12.0x 'defendable' band and the eighteen-month return above 20 percent (20.7 percent a year in the 12.0x branch). On this reading 10 percent earnings growth plus a 5 percent dividend plus a re-rating gives 20 percent a year, and the valuation risk we weight is a sector-wide risk that belongs in portfolio construction, not in the case rating; a crisp, simple, well-guided, low-risk compounding bank with a cash-plus-buyback yield near 9 percent is exactly what the 'Compounder' pattern describes, and the mis-modelled line is real and quantified, so the setup is a B, not a C.

What the record concedes: the franchise quality, the cash yield, the guidance record and the near-term rate tailwind are all real; the ten-year percentile of 65 is a fair corrective to the five-year 96th; on every operating dimension the case is above the comparison set; the multiple's industry character is a fair point; there is a mechanism with a disclosed sensitivity, more than "consensus looks low"; and a Strategy 2030 return target above 18 percent is the one dated event that could change the modal multiple, which is why it is the record's upside trigger.
triggers: - Progress triggers: price at about EUR 9.50 with the deposit beta at or below 25 percent (the eighteen-month modal path clears 20 percent a year; EUR 8.50 for the three-year path); or Strategy 2030 targets on 10 March 2027 setting a return on tangible equity above 18 percent, which would argue the multiple can hold and the modal return moves to the D-to-C range at today's price. A target at or below 15 percent is the alarm on the same event.

- Invalidate as a candidate: deposit beta above 30 percent, or quarterly net interest margin below 2.55 percent. Alarm: beta 25 percent; margin 2.60 percent; non-interest-bearing current accounts down more than 5 percent in a half (the research's own re-run trigger is a beta above 20 percent within two quarters).

- Capital return: alarm on distribution guidance below EUR 2bn a year (March 2027 without a stated offset); invalidate on a regulatory halt to distributions; watch model reviews that could inflate risk weights on real estate and EBS mortgages, the internal-ratings-based transition and the EUR 2.5bn significant risk transfer.
- Multiple: alarm below 9.2x; the sector's own-history percentiles (most of the 95 peers at 80 to 99) as the read-across series; a sector de-rating settles the held-or-drift branch the other way.

- Rates: twelve-month Euribor against the 2.50 percent assumption; a fall back below 2 percent refutes; a curve 50 to 100 basis points above persisting into 2027 and 2028 is the unpriced upside (3 to 6 percent of EPS).

- Credit: cost of risk toward 40 basis points or Stage 2 migration above EUR 1bn as alarm; above 50 basis points halts voluntary distributions (invalidate); the adverse drop-through case in the record uses 45 basis points.
